summary: p95 latency regression in eu-west after enabling tiered batching defaults canary
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer reports increased p95 latency for streaming chat completions in eu-west that started during Redwood canary rollout of tiered batching defaults (runtime 1.22 train).

Customer impact:
- Northlake reports p95 latency increased from ~1.3s to ~2.4s (their app-level measurement: “time to first token”) on their primary streaming endpoint.
- Impact is isolated to eu-west. us-east appears normal per customer.
- Customer states they did not change client settings; regression correlates with our canary enablement window.

Customer environment:
- Product: Hosted API
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (streaming=true)
- Model: rw-llama-70b-instruct
- Region: eu-west
- Tier: customer did not explicitly set batching tier; traffic subject to default policy during canary.

What changed / suspected trigger:
- Tiered batching defaults canary enabled for a small subset of Hosted API routes in eu-west on 2026-04-03 ~09:10 UTC (feature flag rollout).
- Initial suspicion: scheduler heuristic + max-wait budgeting under mixed prompt length distribution causing decode stalls (streaming p95).

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Route ~5% of rw-llama-70b-instruct streaming traffic in eu-west through tiered batching defaults (standard tier default).
2) Send mixed workload: 70% short prompts (<=512 prompt tokens), 30% long prompts (>=4k prompt tokens), concurrency ramp 10 -> 50.
3) Observe:
   - Increased queue depth / higher wait time before first decode step for some requests.
   - p95 “ttft” increases disproportionately vs p50.

Initial data points / customer examples:
- Customer provided approximate request window: 2026-04-03 09:20–10:05 UTC.
- Customer notes regression is worse during local business hours when concurrency is higher.

Redwood investigation notes (SRE/runtime):
- Dashboard review (tier breakdown, queue depth) indicates elevated scheduler wait time and batch formation delays for streaming traffic in eu-west for rw-llama-70b-instruct when tiered defaults are on.
- No significant increase in 5xx or rate limiting (429) observed; this appears performance-only.
- Tail behavior points to starvation/priority inversion under mixed prefill load: long-prefill requests occupying prefill slots and pushing out short requests that should start decode quickly.

Mitigation plan (proposed):
- Immediate: remove Northlake from the canary cohort in eu-west (route override) OR disable tiered defaults canary for the impacted model/region while we validate profile changes.
- Short-term: apply fast-tier tail-latency protections (tighter wait budget, admission control) for streaming routes, or pin streaming routes to fast tier by policy.
- Longer-term: adjust prefill/decode balancing for this model family in eu-west and rerun perf suite mixed-workload scenarios before re-enabling canary.

Requested from customer:
- Confirm whether they can temporarily pin to fast tier for the affected route (we can provide header/config guidance) and whether they can share their prompt length distribution (approx buckets) to confirm similarity to our reproduced case.
comments:
2026-04-03 10:14 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE) — Internal triage
- Confirmed canary change window overlaps with reported regression.
- Pulled eu-west latency panels: p95 TTFT up ~70–90% for cohort; p50 stable.
- Opened #incidents thread for coordination and added Northlake as customer-impacting.

Next: ask runtime scheduling oncall to check queueing/backpressure metrics and whether streaming routes were assigned standard tier by default.

2026-04-03 10:22 UTC — Support (via Aisha) — Customer-facing response
Thanks for reporting. We’re investigating a latency regression in eu-west that may coincide with a canary configuration change on our side. In the meantime, can you confirm:
1) Are you using streaming=true on /v1/chat/completions?
2) Any model/version pins or routing policies set?
3) Any timestamped examples where TTFT was high?
We’ll update within 60 minutes with mitigation options.

2026-04-03 11:01 UTC — Sofia Ivanova (EM Scheduling) — Investigation
Findings:
- In eu-west cohort, batch size distribution is higher variance; some batches skew to long-prefill requests.
- For streaming, “first token” depends on getting into decode quickly; current standard-tier profile in canary allows slightly longer queue wait to form batches.
Hypothesis:
- Under mixed lengths, prefill becomes a bottleneck. The scheduler is not sufficiently prioritizing short streaming requests once long-prefill starts filling prefill budget.
Recommendation:
- For streaming routes, enforce fast-tier wait budget OR introduce a streaming-specific cap on max_wait_ms even when customer is on standard.

2026-04-03 11:18 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Mitigation executed
- Removed Northlake API key from tiered-defaults canary cohort in eu-west (route override in rollout config).
- Monitoring: p95 TTFT for their traffic should normalize within ~10–15 minutes as traffic drains.
- Left canary enabled for other tenants while we validate a safer streaming policy, but marked eu-west + rw-llama-70b-instruct as “watch closely”.

2026-04-03 11:44 UTC — Customer (Northlake) — Confirmation
We’re seeing TTFT back closer to baseline (~1.2–1.5s p95) in eu-west since ~11:30 UTC. No client changes on our side. Yes, streaming=true. We don’t currently set any tier header/policy; we rely on Redwood defaults.

2026-04-04 09:06 UTC — Omar El-Sayed (Runtime) — Root cause + proposed fix
Root cause (most likely):
- Standard-tier profile’s wait budget + prefill/decode balancing allows prefill queue accumulation during concurrency ramps.
- In mixed prompt lengths, long-prefill requests increase time-to-first-decode for unrelated short streaming requests.
- Starvation prevention in fast tier exists, but standard tier does not yet enforce the same streaming-specific guardrail.
Fix proposal:
- Add a streaming guardrail: cap max_wait_ms and tighten admission when streaming=true even under standard tier, and/or default streaming endpoints to fast tier unless customer opts out.
Validation:
- Run benchmark-lab mixed-workload scenario for streaming in eu-west hardware class for rw-llama-70b-instruct; gate on p95/p99 TTFT.

2026-04-05 16:27 UTC — Allison Grant (Observability) — Notes
- Verified tier-labeled panels correctly distinguish cohort vs non-cohort traffic.
- No evidence of elevated errors; only queueing and TTFT.
- Added temporary alert: fast/standard tier TTFT p95 delta > 20% vs baseline for rw-llama-70b-instruct in eu-west (ticket-only, no paging) until canary completes.

2026-04-06 08:40 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Resolution update to customer
We identified the regression as a side effect of a canary batching profile interacting with mixed prompt lengths for streaming workloads. We’ve removed your tenant from the eu-west canary cohort, which is why metrics returned to baseline. We’re updating the canary policy so streaming endpoints receive tighter tail-latency protections before re-expanding rollout.
If you’d like additional control, we can share how to explicitly select the “fast” tier for this route during peak hours.

2026-04-06 09:15 UTC — Customer (Northlake) — Acknowledgement
Thanks. Please send the guidance to force fast tier for our streaming route; we want to be able to pin it during seasonal peaks.
resolution: Mitigated by removing the affected customer tenant from the tiered-batching-defaults canary cohort in eu-west (rollout override). Customer-confirmed p95 TTFT returned to baseline within ~15 minutes. Root cause attributed to standard-tier batching wait budget + prefill/decode balancing under mixed prompt lengths for streaming, causing tail latency inflation. Follow-up work planned to add streaming-specific tail protections to standard tier and to update canary gating for mixed-workload streaming scenarios prior to re-enabling in eu-west.
next_steps: Send customer-facing instructions to force fast tier for streaming route (reference SUP-48244 guidance).
Update rollout criteria: block canary expansion in eu-west for rw-llama-70b-instruct until mixed-workload streaming benchmark passes p95/p99 TTFT gates.
Consider policy change: default streaming endpoints to fast tier unless explicitly configured otherwise (PM sign-off required).
Track baseline refresh after legitimate improvements (INT-33055) so alerts reflect new steady state.
